label: Power BI tables
info: Writes the Power BI shaped tables of site Hull to the data lake, from the files of the fact flow and the reference flow. No call to Insights Hub. Needs the Config tab.

name: [1] TRIGGERS & SETTINGS
info: STAGE 1 - TRIGGERS AND SETTINGS. Site Hull. Schedule: daily at 30 7 * * * (UTC), 30 minutes after the fact flow. Backfill: edit the inject payload {"start":"YYYY-MM-DD","end":"YYYY-MM-DD"} (production days) and click the button. 1.1 is the only node to edit: site name, dry-run switch, rebuild days, calendar range. The shared settings come from the Config tab. dryRun is true by default. 1.2 sends ONE MESSAGE PER DAY (one per 5 s). 1.3 builds the calendar table once per run. This flow only READS files from the data lake that the fact flow and the reference flow wrote. It never calls Insights Hub.

name: [2] LOAD REFERENCE
info: STAGE 2 - one message per day. 2.1 sets the path of dim_asset, the read object node loads the file and the parquet node turns it into rows. 2.2 keeps the rows and sets the path of dim_shift, 2.3 keeps them and sets the path of the day file of fact_kpi. A file that does not exist only gives a warning in the debug sidebar and the day stops here (the read node sends nothing).

name: [3] LOAD FACTS
info: STAGE 3 - reads the day file of fact_kpi and then of fact_loss, with the same pattern. After the last file all four tables of the day are in the message (msg.tables).

name: [4] BUILD TABLES
info: STAGE 4 - the Power BI rows of the day. 4.1 groups the hourly fact_kpi rows to machine x production day x shift (pbi_plan_opt) and to machine x day (pbi_time_utilisation). 4.2 turns every stop into a row of pbi_daily_losses (local time, loss group, sub group, equipment). 4.3 builds one message per table plus the machine names and shift names of the site; in dry-run mode it writes nothing, only a log line. Columns without data in Insights Hub are written as null.

name: [5] WRITE pbi_plan_opt
info: STAGE 5 - parquet node, path and write object for pbi_plan_opt (Plan OPT EU: machine x production day x shift). A rerun replaces the file. Types: UTF8 (STRING), INT64, DOUBLE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS. Dates are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: [6] WRITE pbi_time_utilisation
info: STAGE 6 - parquet node, path and write object for pbi_time_utilisation (Time Utilisation EU: machine x day). A rerun replaces the file. Types: UTF8 (STRING), INT64, DOUBLE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS. Dates are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: [7] WRITE pbi_daily_losses
info: STAGE 7 - parquet node, path and write object for pbi_daily_losses (Daily Losses EU: one row per stop). A rerun replaces the file. Types: UTF8 (STRING), INT64, DOUBLE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS. Dates are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: [8] WRITE pbi_machine_names
info: STAGE 8 - parquet node, path and write object for pbi_machine_names (Machine Names EU: one row per machine). A rerun replaces the file. Types: UTF8 (STRING), INT64, DOUBLE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS. Dates are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: [9] WRITE pbi_shift_naming
info: STAGE 9 - parquet node, path and write object for pbi_shift_naming (Shift Naming EU: one row per shift). A rerun replaces the file. Types: UTF8 (STRING), INT64, DOUBLE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS. Dates are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: [10] WRITE pbi_calendar
info: STAGE 10 - parquet node, path and write object for pbi_calendar (Calendar: one row per date). A rerun replaces the file. Types: UTF8 (STRING), INT64, DOUBLE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS. Dates are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: [11] ERRORS
info: STAGE 11 - a catch node takes every error raised by a node of this tab and turns it into a log line with the name of the node and the message of the API (for example the limit message of evaluateKPIs). Errors of the log nodes themselves are not logged again.

name: [12] LOG
info: STAGE 12 - every log line arrives here through the link "to LOG". 1 turns a line into a row (time, flow, site, production day, level) and shows it in the debug sidebar. The join collects the rows for 30 s, the delay lets one batch pass every 10 s so two writes do not overlap, 3 sets the file of the month and the read node loads the old file. A read of a file that does not exist answers nothing (only a warning), so the same batch also goes through a 10 s wait to the append step. The log is written whatever the dry-run switch says.

name: [13] LOG WRITE
info: STAGE 13 - adds the rows of the batch to the old file and writes the whole file back (the data lake has no append). Columns: ts_utc, seq, flow, site, production_day, mode, level, source, message. Every field is quoted, line breaks become a space. The batch arrives twice (read answer and the wait) and is written once. If the read gives no answer for a file this flow wrote before, a new file with a time stamp is written, so the history is never replaced.
